items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the general municipal law, in relation to electronic bell jar games
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S994

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to electronic
bell jar games

 PURPOSE :

To authorize the use of electronic bell jar devices by charitable
organizations.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Amends subdivision 3a of section 186 of the General
Municipal Law by authorizing bell jar ticket vending machines.

Section 2: Amends section 195-n of the General Municipal Law by adding
a new subdivision 1-a which requires that all manufacturers of bell
jar ticket vending machines who wish to distribute the devices in New
York State receive a license from the New York State Gaming Commission
and that the Commission approve an identical version of the device
before the manufacturer can distribute it.

Section 3: Renumbers subdivision 2 of section 195-q of the General
Municipal Law as subdivision 3 and adds a new subdivision 2 which
imposes restrictions, reporting requirements and fees upon
manufacturers and authorized organizations that use electronic bell
jar devices.

Section 4: Effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill seeks to provide a more entertaining form of a "bell jar"
game that has been a popular fundraising device for charitable and
fraternal organizations for over twenty-five years. The electronic
form of this game will also inhibit the purchase of illegal bell jar
tickets and the manipulation of the outcome of bell jar games and
provide state-of-the-art accounting devices that will provide
regulators with assurances that bell jar games are conducted in
accordance with law.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S.1371-B of 2016: Passed Senate, Died in Assembly Racing and Wagering.
S.1371-A of 2015: Died in Senate Finance, Died in Assembly Racing and
Wagering.
S.1889 of 2014: Died on Senate Floor Calendar, Died in Assembly Racing
and Wagering
S.1889 of 2013: Died in Senate Finance, Died in Assembly Racing and
Wagering
S.6961 of 2012: Died in Senate Finance, Died in Assembly Racing and
Wagering

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Potential for enhanced revenues to the state through licensing fees
and from charitable gaming.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S994A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to electronic
bell jar games

 PURPOSE :

To authorize the use of electronic bell jar vending machines by
authorized charitable organizations.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Establishes legislative findings and purpose.

Section 2: Authorizes and defines electronic bell jar vending machines
for the purpose of conducting bell jar games.

Section 3: Prohibits any electronic bell jar vending machine to be
sold, leased, distributed, installed, or operated until approved by
the New York State Gaming Commission.

Section 4: Prohibits any charitable organization from purchasing or
leasing any electronic bell jar vending machine from any manufacturer
or distributor that is not licensed by the New York State Gaming
Commission.

Section 5: Establishes the license fee for manufacturers of electronic
bell jar vending machines.

Section 6: Establishes the operational requirements for electronic
bell jar vending machines.

Section 7: Prohibits any manufacturer from selling any electronic bell
jar vending machine to any distributor that is not licensed by the New
York State Gaming Commission; and requires manufacturers to report to
the New York State Gaming Commission any electronic bell jar vending
machine sold or leased to a distributor.

Section 8: Prohibits any distributor from purchasing any electronic
bell jar vending machine from any manufacturer that is not licensed by
the New York State Gaming Commission; and requires distributors to
maintain records of all electronic bell jar vending machines that it
sells or leases and to report such information to the New York State
Gaming Commission.

Section 9: Establishes additional requirements and compliance
standards for electronic bell jar vending machines.

Section 10: Effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill seeks to provide a more entertaining form of a "bell jar"
vending machine that has been a popular fundraising device for
charitable and fraternal organizations. The electronic form of this
vending machine will also inhibit the purchase of illegal bell jar
tickets and the manipulation of the outcome of bell jar games and
provide state-of-the-art accounting devices that will provide
regulators with assurances that bell jar games are conducted in
accordance with law.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S.1371-B of 2016: Passed Senate, Died in Assembly Racing and Wagering.
S.1371-A of 2015: Died in Senate Finance, Died in Assembly Racing and
Wagering.
S.1889 of 2014: Died on Senate Floor Calendar, Died in Assembly Racing
and Wagering
S.1889 of 2013: Died in Senate Finance, Died in Assembly Racing and
Wagering
S.6961 of 2012: Died in Senate Finance, Died in Assembly Racing and
Wagering

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Potential for enhanced revenues to the state through licensing fees
and from charitable gaming.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

BILL NUMBER: S994B

SPONSOR: BONACIC
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation
to electronic bell jar games

 
PURPOSE:

To authorize the use of electronic bell jar vending machines by author-
ized charitable organizations.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1:  Establishes legislative findings and purpose.

Section 2:  Authorizes and defines electronic bell jar vending machines
for the purpose of conducting bell jar games.

Section 3:  Prohibits any electronic bell jar vending machine to be
sold, leased, distributed, installed, or operated until approved by the
New York State Gaming Commission.

Section 4:  Prohibits any charitable organization from purchasing or
leasing any electronic bell jar vending machine from any manufacturer or
distributor that is not licensed by the New York State Gaming Commis-
sion.

Section 5:  Establishes the license fee for manufacturers of electronic
bell jar vending machines.

Section 6:  Establishes the operational requirements for electronic bell
jar vending machines.

Section 7:  Prohibits any manufacturer from selling any electronic bell
jar vending machine to any distributor that is not licensed by the New
York State Gaming Commission; and requires manufacturers to report to
the New York State Gaming Commission any electronic bell jar vending
machine sold or leased to a distributor.

Section 8:  Prohibits any distributor from purchasing any electronic
bell jar vending machine from any manufacturer that is not licensed by
the New York State Gaming Commission; and requires distributors to main-
tain records of all electronic bell jar vending machines that it sells
or leases and to report such information to the New York State Gaming
Commission.

Section 9:  Establishes additional requirements and compliance standards
for electronic bell jar vending machines. Additionally, this section
limits the number of electronic bell jar vending machines than an
authorized organization may operate to no more than ten unless the
organization is located in a Native American exclusivity area, in which
they are limited to no more than five machines. Finally, this section
provides that an authorized organization must be licensed to operate
games of chance for at least five years prior to being authorized to
operate electronic bell jar vending machines unless the location is
located in a Native American exclusivity area, in which an organization
must have been licensed to operate games of chance prior to the effec-
tive date of this legislation in order to be authorized to operate elec-
tronic bell jar vending machines.
Section 10:  Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill seeks to provide a more entertaining form of a "bell jar"
vending machine that has been a popular fundraising device for charita-
ble and fraternal organizations. The electronic form of this vending
machine will also inhibit the purchase of illegal bell jar tickets and
the manipulation of the outcome of bell jar games and provide state-of-
the-art accounting devices that will provide regulators with assurances
that bell jar games are conducted in accordance with law.

Potential for enhanced revenues to the state through licensing fees and
from charitable gaming.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 351
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 994-C, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the general municipal law, in relation to electron-
      ic bell jar games"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would authorize the use of electronic bell jars by organiza-
tions licensed to offer games of chance.
 
  In  2013,  voters approved by referendum an amendment to the Constitu-
tion allowing for casino gambling. That amendment limited casino  gambl-
ing  to seven locations and recognized the need for ample protections to
ensure that charitable gaming  does  not  become  commercialized.  These
electronic bell jar machines are visually identical to slot machines and
this bill runs the risk of blurring the line between commercial gambling
and a charitable endeavor.
 
  This bill would also apply to any authorized organization that holds a
game  of chance license and who previously conducted non-electronic bell
jar games. While there are  records  of  those  entities  who  currently
conduct  bell  jar games, there is no way to confirm if an entity previ-
ously conducted these games.  Therefore,  this  bill  would  effectively
apply  to any authorized organization that holds a game of chance. There
are almost 11,000 such organizations statewide. Since each entity  would
be  allowed to operate up to 5 machines on their premises, this provides
a potential operation of 55,000 machines throughout the state.
 
  Currently, by contrast, there are approximately 18,500  video  lottery
terminals throughout the state. The machines produce revenue of approxi-
mately  two  billion  dollars  each  year,  of  which approximately $950
million goes directly to education. The same number of  electronic  bell
jar  machines  placed  throughout  the state at authorized organizations
could generate upwards of $625 million dollars, zero of which  would  go
directly  to  education. Further, it is inevitable that several of these
machines would be located within close proximity to video lottery termi-
nals, thus competing for their business and lowering the amount that our
educational system would receive.
 
  Additionally, this bill has a fatal technical flaw. The Gaming Compact
between the State of New York and the Seneca Nation of Indians prohibits
the use of "slot machines" within an exclusivity zone  by  anyone  other
than  a  member  of the Nation. These machines would likely constitute a
"slot machine" under the definition  established  in  the  Compact,  and
their  placement within the exclusivity zone could result in a breach of
the Compact by the State. Based upon these and other  considerations,  I
cannot  support  this  bill.  However,  because I recognize the needs of
charitable organizations to increase their  revenue  so  that  they  can
continue  to  provide  invaluable  social  services to their members and
communities, I will have my staff undertake discussions with the  Legis-
lature during the upcoming budget negotiations to determine if there are
any viable solutions.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
